name: reconcile-public-install
body: source: change request "public-install" — really-knows-ai/kalide is now PUBLIC (private was always temporary). inconsistency: the spec required private-repo distribution: HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN + a custom Homebrew download strategy (Formula/lib/github_private_release_download_strategy.rb), a KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN Scoop pre_install workaround, docs explaining repo access and token setup, git-access-based tap/bucket, and "private repo" wording across requirements, domain and solution nodes and workflow comments. resolution: token/private requirements rewritten (not removed, identities kept) to anonymous public install: homebrew-install (plain release-download url+sha256, no strategy, strategy file removed), scoop-install (standard architecture 64bit/arm64 url+hash, no pre_install, bucket/README.md updated), tap-bucket-location (public HTTPS, no credentials), package-manifest-update (release.yml regenerates the public forms), install-docs (no token/account; INSTALL.md the detailed guide), linux-install (anonymous download; manual download also the macOS/Windows fallback), readme-presentation (AC no longer demands a token step), source-repo/distribution/github-releases/supported-platforms/native-ci-verification (public wording; native-ci AC forbids private-repo comments in ci.yml/native-e2e.yml/release.yml), stakeholder kalide-maintainers; domain release/install-kalide/package-manifest; solution homebrew-formula/scoop-manifest/install-docs/release-workflow/release-pipeline/native-e2e-ci/package-channels. Added requirements.requirement.readme-install-front-loading (Homebrew + Scoop first in README Install, manual download as Linux/fallback) and global.constraint.anonymous-install. Added implemented-by: scoop-manifest→bucket/kalide.json, bucket/README.md; install-docs→INSTALL.md; release-pipeline→.github/workflows/ci.yml. Supersedes the token/private parts of requirements.note.distribution-decisions (item 3) and requirements.note.tap-bucket-location-open ("reuse existing git access"). kalide-rename still lists `KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN` only as an example of the KALIDE_* prefix; that is naming history, not a requirement to use a token. [with user]
